delete.description: Deletes a message: it is removed from every list and conversation at once, its attachments are removed from your file library within 48 hours, and the delete is recorded with who made it. The phone is also asked to delete its own copy, asynchronously. The response returns at once with the deleted message as GET /messages/{message_id} returns it (deleted_at set, no body or parts), with phone_deletion.status pending while the phone has not answered. Axilio keeps checking for up to 7 days, asking the phone again until it confirms; phone_deletion.next_check_at is when it next checks (null once the outcome is final). A phone not yet set up to delete messages (not_default_app) is asked once it can, within those 7 days. GET /messages/{message_id} keeps returning the deleted message and shows where the phone's copy stands in phone_deletion. Webhooks: message.deleted fires at once; message.phone_deleted fires when the phone holds no copy, and message.phone_delete_failed when it is final that the copy is still there or may be (ambiguous, not_matched, not_sent, or unconfirmed after the 7 days). A message the phone stored before it became the phone's messaging app can only be deleted on the phone when it is a plain text the phone can match, and only on the first attempt; otherwise the phone answers not_matched. Deleting a message the phone is still sending does not stop the send. Deleting a message that does not exist or is already deleted is a 404.

get.description: Streams a session's telemetry as Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream): every frame of the canonical envelope GET /phones/sessions/{session_id}/frames returns, live as the session runs. Each event's id is its resume cursor, its event name is the frame kind (span or log), and its data is the frame JSON; live spans arrive as a start frame and then an end frame. A new reader (or one whose cursor is older than the live window) first receives the archived trace and then the live frames, deduplicated on span id and phase, followed by an event with no data that carries the cursor the replay ended at. Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header (EventSource sends it on its own) to resume with no gap. A comment line is sent every 15 seconds while the stream is idle. After the session ends the stream serves what is left and closes; a reconnect with nothing left after its cursor gets 204, which tells EventSource to stop. Authenticate with the API key header, or open the session's telemetry_url, which carries a read-only token for this one session (for browsers, which cannot set headers on an EventSource). A session started with telemetry off streams nothing (409). Org-scoped: another org's session reads as not found. The stream is served by the realtime service: telemetry_url points at its host, and this path on the API host is routed there too. Each event carries exactly one frame. Readers MUST ignore events with an unknown name, unknown fields, and unknown span_type or log_type values.
